standard_prerequisites.name: Grothendieck-Serre duality for projectively embeddable morphisms
standard_prerequisites.statement: For a projectively embeddable morphism f from X to Y of noetherian schemes of finite Krull dimension there exist an exceptional inverse image functor f^!, a trace map Tr from Rf_* f^! to 1 in D^+_qc(Y) and the adjunction theta from Rf_* R-Hom_X(F, f^!G) to R-Hom_Y(Rf_*F, G); the author restates exactly this as Theorem 3.2 at source lines 659-669 and its retained proof at 671-673 is the author's own pointer to Hartshorne, Residues and duality, Th. III.8.7, III.10.5 and III.11.1.
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the quasi-isomorphism Rf_*(F-dual tensored with omega^circ)[1] = R-Hom over O_K of (Rf_*F, O_K) used at source lines 758-761; the counted proof does not reprove it.

standard_prerequisites.name: Pontryagin duality over the valuation ring
standard_prerequisites.statement: For the discrete valuation ring O_K with fraction field K and a finite O_K-module M, the natural map from M to Hom over O_K of (Hom over O_K of (M, K/O_K), K/O_K) is an isomorphism; in the notation of the counted proof this reads Hom over O_K of (ker(d tensored with 1), K/O_K) = coker(d-dual).
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the identification of the two displayed two-term complexes into the perfect pairing asserted by the counted proposition (source line 762).

core_obligations: Show that Rf_*F for a locally free F of finite rank on an lci projective curve f: X to Spec O_K is representable by a perfect complex concentrated in degrees 0 and 1, using projectivity and finite generation over O_K (source lines 748-751).

Replace F by F tensored with K/O_K and identify Rf_* of (F tensored with K/O_K) with the two-term complex M_0 tensored with K/O_K mapping to M_1 tensored with K/O_K of free O_K-modules (source lines 752-756).

Apply the retained Grothendieck-Serre duality to obtain the quasi-isomorphism Rf_*(F-dual tensored with omega^circ)[1] = R-Hom over O_K of (Rf_*F, O_K) and read off the dual two-term complex M_1-dual mapping to M_0-dual (source lines 758-761).

Convert the resulting identification of kernels and cokernels into the perfect pairing from H^0(X, F tensored with K/O_K) times H^1(X, F-dual tensored with omega^circ) to K/O_K by Pontryagin duality (source line 762).

proof_roadmap.step: Rf_*F is a perfect complex of length [0,1].
Compute Rf_* of (F tensored with K/O_K) by the two-term complex of free modules.
Dualize with the retained Grothendieck-Serre duality to get the dual complex.
Apply Pontryagin duality to obtain the perfect pairing.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is Proposition 3.7 at source lines 732-745, label LocalDualityCurves: for an lci projective curve f: X to Spec O_K and a locally free F of finite rank it asserts that Rf_*F is a perfect complex of length [0,1] and that cup product with the trace gives a perfect pairing from H^0(X, F tensored with K/O_K) times H^1(X, F-dual tensored with omega^circ) to K/O_K. The proof at source lines 747-763 must build the two-term free complex, replace F by F tensored with K/O_K so that the K/O coefficients compute Rf_* of (F tensored with K/O_K), and then dualize through the retained Grothendieck-Serre adjunction into R-Hom over O_K of (Rf_*F, O_K). The step that is not a routine check is the final Pontryagin-duality conversion Hom over O_K of (ker(d tensored with 1), K/O_K) = coker(d-dual) at source line 762, which is what upgrades a quasi-isomorphism of complexes into perfectness of the pairing over the non-field ring O_K. The argument is short once that conversion is seen, so the card is rated H2.
